title: Polynomial description of a partial Popescu chart after killing pi
statement: Let R and Cbar be commutative rings, pi in R, and d compatible prepared polynomial data as in [lem-weil-pbc-popescu-lift-preparation]. Put R2=R/(pi^2), A=((R2)[x]/(reduced f_l)) localized at reduced a_k. Let B be a commutative R2-algebra with compatible R-algebra structure and with pi mapping to zero. Fix k. Put u_l=f_l-pi*z_l and p_kl=a_k*z_l-sum_{j in E_k}h_klj*z_j-pi*g_kl in R[x,z]. Let F_l be any family equal to the renaming by finSumFinEquiv of u_l for l in E_k and p_kl otherwise. Put S=R[Fin(n+m)]/(F_l), and let s be the quotient class of the similarly renamed a_k. Then the localization of B tensor_R S at 1 tensor s [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property, def-weil-ring-localization-away] is isomorphic, as a B-algebra, to the polynomial ring [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring] in card(E_k) variables over B tensor_R2 A. This is only the algebra calculation, with no claim about smoothness, differential rank, dimension, flatness or the full lifting algebra.

source.place: Stacks Project, Tag 07CP (lemma-lifting), displayed calculation of (D_k/pi D_k) localized at a_k; read at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/07CP because the local TeX is absent.

proof.text: Use finSumFinEquiv to rename the ambient variables. Every partial relation lies in the ideal J generated by all original equations u_l and all equations p_kl of the fixed chart. Inverse renaming followed by the quotient map therefore gives a surjective R-algebra map from the given partial quotient S to ULift(Q/J).

In L=(B tensor_R S)[1/a_k], pi is zero and each selected original relation gives f_j=0. Map the prepared identity a_k f_l=sum h_klj f_j+pi^2 g_kl into L. Its right side is zero and a_k is a unit, hence every f_l is zero. Every u_l therefore vanishes. For l outside E_k the relation p_kl already belongs to the partial ideal; for l in E_k normalization makes p_kl identically zero even before base change. Thus all of J vanishes in L.

Extend the surjective quotient map with B. Algebra.TensorProduct.lTensor_ker expresses its kernel as the ideal generated by the image of the original kernel, and the preceding vanishing shows that this ideal maps to zero in L. IsLocalization.Away.map_injective_iff and map_eq_zero_iff then prove the localized map injective; map_surjective_of_surjective proves it surjective. This gives a B-algebra equivalence between the localized partial and single-chart quotients.

Apply the existing zero-base single-chart polynomial theorem with the prepared normalized coefficients. Identify the localized elements through the quotient map, compose with the inverse localized equivalence, and reindex the free variables by (E_k).equivFin.symm. This gives the required B-algebra equivalence without introducing any additional theorem with sorry.

proof_origin.note: B4: compare the partial quotient with the existing zero-base single-chart polynomial theorem by a localized surjection. The omitted original relations vanish by the prepared identity; the omitted selected auxiliary relations are identically zero by normalization. lean.statement:
theorem popescu_partial_chart_polynomial (R : Type a) (Cbar : Type c)
    [CommRing R] [CommRing Cbar] [Algebra R Cbar] (π : R)
    [Algebra (R ⧸ Ideal.span ({π ^ 2} : Set R)) Cbar]
    [IsScalarTower R (R ⧸ Ideal.span ({π ^ 2} : Set R)) Cbar]
    (d : PopescuLiftPresentation R Cbar π) (hd : d.Prepared)
    (B : Type b) [CommRing B] [Algebra R B]
    [Algebra (R ⧸ Ideal.span ({π ^ 2} : Set R)) B]
    [IsScalarTower R (R ⧸ Ideal.span ({π ^ 2} : Set R)) B]
    (hπ : algebraMap R B π = 0) (k : Fin d.r)
    (F : Fin d.m → MvPolynomial (Fin (d.n + d.m)) R)
    (hF : ∀ l, F l = MvPolynomial.rename finSumFinEquiv
      (if l ∈ d.E k then d.equation (.inl l) else d.equation (.inr (k, l)))) :
    let S := MvPolynomial (Fin (d.n + d.m)) R ⧸ Ideal.span (Set.range F)
    let s : S := Ideal.Quotient.mk _
      (MvPolynomial.rename finSumFinEquiv (d.includeX (d.a k)))
    Nonempty (MvPolynomial (Fin (d.E k).card)
      (B ⊗[R ⧸ Ideal.span ({π ^ 2} : Set R)]
        Localization.Away (d.reducedElement k)) ≃ₐ[B]
      Localization.Away (Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight (R := R) (A := B) s))
